1.word_for_word: त्रयस्त्रिंशे ततो गोपी-मण्डली मध्यगो हरिः । — At the thirty-third place, the Lord Hari appeared in the middle of the group of gopīs.; प्रियास् ता रमयामास ह्रदिनी-वन-केलिभिः ॥ — His beloved entertained her with his playful activities in the lakes and forests.; तत् तदा अङ्ग हे राजन् ! — That then limb, O king!; यद् वा, तस्य भगवतोऽङ्गेन वपुषा कर-चरणाद्य्-अवयवैर् वा उपचिताः समृद्धा आशिषो यासां ताः ॥१॥ — Whatever blessings are accumulated by the body, hands, feet and other parts of the body of the Supreme Personality of Godhead are enriched.; : यद् वा, तासां गोपीनाम् अङ्गैर् उपचिता आशिषो यस्य । — or, whose blessings are accumulated by the limbs of those gopīs.
1.translation: At the thirty-third place, the Lord Hari appeared in the middle of the group of gopīs. His beloved entertained her with his playful activities in the lakes and forests. That then limb, O king! Whatever blessings are accumulated by the body, hands, feet and other parts of the body of the Supreme Personality of Godhead are enriched. or, whose blessings are accumulated by the limbs of those gopīs.

2.word_for_word:
रास-क्रीडां रासो नाम बहु-नर्तकी-युक्तो नृत्य-विशेषः, तां क्रीडाम् । — The game of Rasa Rasa is a special dance with many dancers, that game.; अन्योन्यम् आबद्धाः संग्रथिता बाहवो यैस् तैः सह ॥२॥ — They were bound together and their arms were joined together.; : "नतैर् गृहीतकण्ठानाम् अन्योन्यात्तकरश्रियम् । — "The beauty of the hands of those who bowed down and held their necks together.; नर्तकीनां भवेद्
रासो मण्डलीभूय नर्तनम् ॥" इति रासलक्षणम् । — It should be for dancers
Raso is dancing in a circle. This is the characteristic of Rasa.
2.translation:
The game of Rasa Rasa is a special dance with many dancers, that game. They were bound together and their arms were joined together. "The beauty of the hands of those who bowed down and held their necks together. It should be for dancers
Raso is dancing in a circle. This is the characteristic of Rasa.

3-4.word_for_word: तत्-साहित्यम् अभिनयेन दर्शयति---रासोत्सव इत्य् अक्षर-अवरुद्ध्प्रविष्टेन तेनैव कण्ठे गृहीतानाम् उभयत आलिङ्गितानाम् । — He acts out that literature by entering the letters Rasotsav and embracing them on both sides.; कथंभूतेन ? — By what kind of ?; यं सर्वाः स्त्रियः स्व-निकटं माम् एवाश्लिष्टवान् इति मन्येरंस् तेन एतद् अर्थं द्वयोर् द्वयोर् मध्ये प्रविष्टेनेत्य् अर्थः। — By the one whom all women would think had embraced me close to them, this means that he had entered between two.; नन्व् एकस्य कथं तथा प्रवेशः, सर्व-सन्निहितत्वे वा कुतः स्वैक-निकटत्वाभिमानस् तासाम् इत्य् अत उक्तं---योगेश्वरेणेति । — Now, how can one enter in such a way, or in the presence of all, where is the pride of their being near to oneself?; अचिन्त्य-शक्तिनेत्य् अर्थः ॥३॥ — by the power of the unthinkable.; तावत् तत्-क्षणम् एवौत्सुक्य-व्याप्त-मनसां स-स्त्रीकाणां देवानां विमान-शतैः सङ्कुलं सङ्कीर्णं नभो बभूव ॥४॥ — At that very moment the sky became crowded with hundreds of aerial chariots of the gods along with their wives whose minds were overwhelmed with anxiety
3-4.translation: He acts out that literature by entering the letters Rasotsav and embracing them on both sides. By what kind of ? By the one whom all women would think had embraced me close to them, this means that he had entered between two. Now, how can one enter in such a way, or in the presence of all, where is the pride of their being near to oneself? by the power of the unthinkable. At that very moment the sky became crowded with hundreds of aerial chariots of the gods along with their wives whose minds were overwhelmed with anxiety

5.word_for_word: तत् तस्य भगवतः श्री-कृष्णस्यामलं निर्मलं यशो जगुर् इति ॥५॥ — That is why they chanted the pure and immaculate fame of that Supreme Personality of Godhead, Lord Kṛṣṇa.
5.translation: That is why they chanted the pure and immaculate fame of that Supreme Personality of Godhead, Lord Kṛṣṇa.

6.word_for_word: स-प्रियाणां कृष्ण-सहितानाम् । — He-loved ones with Krishna.; तुमुलः सङ्कीर्णः ॥६॥ — tumultuous and crowded.
6.translation: He-loved ones with Krishna. tumultuous and crowded.

7.word_for_word: महा-मरकतो नील-मणिर् इव हैमानां मणीनां मध्ये मध्ये ताभिः स्वर्ण-वर्णाभिर् आश्लिष्टाभिः शुशुभे । — It shone like a blue jewel from a great emerald, embraced by the golden gems in the middle of the golden gems.; गोपी-दृष्ट्य्-अभिप्रायेण वा विनैव मध्य-पदावृत्तिम् एक-वचनम् ॥७॥ — Without the intention of the gopī’s sight or the intention of the middle foot, the singular is used.
7.translation: It shone like a blue jewel from a great emerald, embraced by the golden gems in the middle of the golden gems. Without the intention of the gopī’s sight or the intention of the middle foot, the singular is used.

8.word_for_word: स यथा ताभिः शुशुभे, तथा ता अपि तेन विरेजुर् इत्य् आह---पाद-न्यासैर् इति । — As he shone with them, so they shone with him, he said, by the placement of their feet.; भुज-विधुतिभिः कर-चालनैर् भज्यमानैर् मध्यैश् चलद्भिः कुचैश् च पटैश् च । — The breasts and fabrics moving in the middle were broken by the lightning movements of the hands; गण्ड-लोलैर् गण्डेषु चञ्चलैः । — They rolled their cheeks and moved their cheeks.; स्विद्यन् मुख्यः स्विद्यन्ति स्वेदम् उद्गिरन्ति मुखानि यासां ताः । — The main person who sweats is the one whose faces are sweaty and whose faces are full of sweat.; कबरेषु रशनासु च ग्रन्थयो दृढा यासाम् । — They have strong knots in their graves and in their belts.; यद् वा, तेषु तासु चाग्रन्थयः, शिथिल-ग्रन्थय इत्य् अर्थः । — That is, there are knots in them and in those knots, loose knots.; तत्र नाना-मूर्तिः कृष्णो मेघ-चक्रम् इव, तास् तु बहु-विधास् तडित इव स्वेदस् तुषार इव, गीतं गर्जितम् एवेति यथा-सम्भवम् ऊह्यम् ॥८॥ — There are various forms of Krishna, like the wheel of clouds, and they are of many kinds, like lightning, sweat and snow, and the song is thunderous, and it is to be understood as much as possible.
8.translation: As he shone with them, so they shone with him, he said, by the placement of their feet. The breasts and fabrics moving in the middle were broken by the lightning movements of the hands They rolled their cheeks and moved their cheeks. The main person who sweats is the one whose faces are sweaty and whose faces are full of sweat. They have strong knots in their graves and in their belts. That is, there are knots in them and in those knots, loose knots. There are various forms of Krishna, like the wheel of clouds, and they are of many kinds, like lightning, sweat and snow, and the song is thunderous, and it is to be understood as much as possible.

9.word_for_word: नृत्यमाना नृत्यन्त्यः । — They danced and danced.; रक्त-कण्ठ्यो नाना-रागैर् अनुरञ्जित-कण्ठ्यः । — He has a red throat and a throat decorated with various melodies.; कृष्णस्याभिमर्शेन संस्पर्शेन मुदिताः । — They were delighted to be touched by the touch of Lord Kṛṣṇa.; इदं विश्वम् ॥९॥ — This is the universe.
9.translation: They danced and danced. He has a red throat and a throat decorated with various melodies. They were delighted to be touched by the touch of Lord Kṛṣṇa. This is the universe.

10.word_for_word: मुकुन्देन सह स्वर-जातीः षड्जादि-स्वरालाप-गतीः । — With Mukunda, the vocal species are the sixth and other vowel conversation movements.; अमिश्रिताः कृष्णोन्नीताभिर् असङ्कीर्णाः । — They are not mixed and are not crowded with black raised materials.; प्रीयमाणेन संमानिता तज्-जात्य्-उन्नयनम् एव ध्रुवं ध्रुवाख्यं ताल-विशेषं कृत्वा उन्निन्ये उन्नीतवती ॥१०॥ — Honored by the delighted one she raised him up by making a special rhythm called Dhruva for the elevation of that race
10.translation: With Mukunda, the vocal species are the sixth and other vowel conversation movements. They are not mixed and are not crowded with black raised materials. Honored by the delighted one she raised him up by making a special rhythm called Dhruva for the elevation of that race

11.word_for_word: एवं नृत्य-गीतादिना श्री-कृष्ण-संमानितानां तासाम् अतिप्रीति-विलसितं वृत्तम् आह---काचिद् इति । — Thus, the story of the women who were honored by Lord Kṛṣṇa by dancing, singing and so on, and who were very pleased with them, is described as follows; श्लथन्ति वलयानि मल्लिकाश् च यस्याः सा ॥११॥ — She whose rings and jasmines are slipping.
11.translation: Thus, the story of the women who were honored by Lord Kṛṣṇa by dancing, singing and so on, and who were very pleased with them, is described as follows She whose rings and jasmines are slipping.

12.word_for_word: उत्पलस्य सौरभं यस्य, तं बाहुम् ॥१२॥ — That arm which has the fragrance of a lotus.
12.translation: That arm which has the fragrance of a lotus.

13.word_for_word:
नाट्येन नृत्येन विक्षिप्तयोश् चञ्चलयोः कुण्डलयोस् त्विषेण त्विषा मण्डितं गण्डं कपोलं तथा-भूते स्व-गण्डे सन्दधत्याः संयोजयन्त्याः ॥१३॥ — Their cheeks, which were adorned with the sparkle of their earrings, were stirred by the theatrical dance, and they were fixed to their own cheeks in the same way.; : नृत्येन विक्षिप्ते चञ्चले कुण्डले च स्वाभाविकी गण्डत्विट् च
तत्समाहारस् त्विषं तेन मण्डितम् इति । — Dancing distracted with shiny earrings and a natural cheek twitch
The combination of that is that the light is adorned with it.; "द्वन्द्वाच् चुदषहान्तात्" इति
टच् । — "from the duality of the chudashahanta
Touch.
13.translation:
Their cheeks, which were adorned with the sparkle of their earrings, were stirred by the theatrical dance, and they were fixed to their own cheeks in the same way. Dancing distracted with shiny earrings and a natural cheek twitch
The combination of that is that the light is adorned with it. "from the duality of the chudashahanta
Touch.

14.word_for_word: कूजती नूपुरे मेखला च यस्याः सा ॥१४॥ — She whose anklets and belt are whistling
14.translation: She whose anklets and belt are whistling

15.word_for_word: एवम् अन्या अपि गोप्यो यथा-यथं नाना-विभ्रमैर् विजह्रुर् इत्य् आह---गोप्य इति ॥१५॥ — Thus the other gopīs also played with various delusions in various ways.
15.translation: Thus the other gopīs also played with various delusions in various ways.

16.word_for_word: तत्र वादकेषु गायकेषु गन्धर्व-किन्नरादिषु रसावेशेन मुह्यत्सु चान्याम् एव वाद्यादि-सम्पत्तिं दर्शयन् रास-संभ्रमम् आह---कर्णोत्पल- इति । — There, among the musicians, singers, Gandharvas, Kinnaras and others, who were bewildered by the attachment of taste, he pointed to another property of musical instruments and other instruments and said that the confusion of taste was called Karnotpala.; कर्णोत्पलैश् च, आलक-विटङ्कैर् अलकालङ्कृतैः कपोलैश् च, घर्मैश् च वक्त्रेषु श्रीः शोभा यासां, ताः । — They are the ones whose earrings are adorned with lotuses, whose foreheads are adorned with alaka and vitanka, and whose faces are adorned with warmth.; घोषाः किङ्किण्यः । — The horses are tinkling.; वलय-नूपुर-घोषैर् वाद्यैर् वादित्रैः स्व-केशेभ्यः स्रस्ताः स्रजो यासां ताः । — They were the ones whose garlands fell from their hair to the sound of rings, anklets and other musical instruments.; एतेन ताल-गति-सन्तुष्टाः केशाः स-शिरः-कम्पं पादेषु पुष्प-वृष्टिम् इवाकुर्वन्न् इत्य् उत्प्रेक्षितम् । — This suggested that the hair, satisfied with the rhythmic movement, was shaking its head as if it were showering flowers on its feet.; भगवता सह ननृतुः । — They danced with the Lord.; क्व ? — Where?; भ्रमरा एव गायका यस्यां रास-सभायाम् ॥१६॥ — The bees are the only singers in that assembly of rāsa.
16.translation: There, among the musicians, singers, Gandharvas, Kinnaras and others, who were bewildered by the attachment of taste, he pointed to another property of musical instruments and other instruments and said that the confusion of taste was called Karnotpala. They are the ones whose earrings are adorned with lotuses, whose foreheads are adorned with alaka and vitanka, and whose faces are adorned with warmth. The horses are tinkling. They were the ones whose garlands fell from their hair to the sound of rings, anklets and other musical instruments. This suggested that the hair, satisfied with the rhythmic movement, was shaking its head as if it were showering flowers on its feet. They danced with the Lord. Where? The bees are the only singers in that assembly of rāsa.

17.word_for_word: यथा गोप्यो नाना-विभ्रमैर् भगवता सह विजह्रुर् एवं भगवान् अपि स्व-विलासैस् ताभिः सह रेम इत्य् आह---एवम् इति । — Just as the gopīs enjoyed themselves with the Lord in various delusions, so the Lord enjoyed Himself with them in His own pleasures.; तद्-विलासानभिभूतस्यैव रतौ दृष्टान्तः---यथार्भक इति । — The illustration of the same person who is overcome by that luxury is as a child.; स्व-प्रतिबिम्बैर् विभ्रमः क्रीडा यस्य, स इव । — It is like a game of confusion in one’s own images.; अनेनैतद् दर्शितम्---स्वीयम् एव सर्व-कला-कौशलं सौगन्ध्य-लावण्य-माधुर्यादि च तासु सञ्चार्य ताभिः सह रेमे, यथार्भकः स्व-प्रतिबिम्बैर् इति ॥१७॥ — This shows that he moved about in them with his own skill in all arts, fragrance, beauty, sweetness and so on, and enjoyed with them, just as a child enjoys with his own images.
17.translation: Just as the gopīs enjoyed themselves with the Lord in various delusions, so the Lord enjoyed Himself with them in His own pleasures. The illustration of the same person who is overcome by that luxury is as a child. It is like a game of confusion in one’s own images. This shows that he moved about in them with his own skill in all arts, fragrance, beauty, sweetness and so on, and enjoyed with them, just as a child enjoys with his own images.

18.word_for_word: तास् तु भगवद्-विलासैर् आकुला बभूवुर् इत्य् आह---तद्-अङ्ग- इति । — They were overwhelmed by the pleasures of the Lord, and he argued that they were part of it.; तस्य अङ्ग-सङ्गेन प्रकृष्टा मुत् प्रीति, तया आकुलान्य् अवशानि इन्द्रियाणि यासां ताः । — Mut love, attracted by the attachment to his limbs, and her senses are overwhelmed by it.; विश्लथ-बन्धान् केशादीन् अञ्जसा प्रतिव्योढुं यथा-पूर्वं धर्तुं नालं न समर्था बभूवुः । — They were unable to easily pull back the loose bonds of hair and other objects and to hold the nails as before.; विस्रस्ता माला आभरणानि च यासां ताः ॥१८॥ — The garlands and ornaments of those women were thrown away; : अञ्जसा अनुसन्धान-पूर्वकम् । — Easily research-oriented.
18.translation: They were overwhelmed by the pleasures of the Lord, and he argued that they were part of it. Mut love, attracted by the attachment to his limbs, and her senses are overwhelmed by it. They were unable to easily pull back the loose bonds of hair and other objects and to hold the nails as before. The garlands and ornaments of those women were thrown away Easily research-oriented.

19.word_for_word: न केवलं ता एवाकुलेन्द्रियाः किन्तु देव्योऽपीत्य् आह---कृष्ण-विक्रीडितम् इति । — Not only are they the same senses but also the goddesses, he argues, because they are played with by Krishna.; किं च शशाङ्कश् चेति । — What about the moon?; अनेनैतत् सूचितम्---शशाङ्केन विस्मितेन गतौ विस्मृतायाम् । — This indicates that the moon was surprised and forgot to go.; ततः प्राक्तनाः सर्वेऽपि ग्रहास् तत्र तत्रैव तस्थुः । — Then all the previous planets remained in the same place.; ततश् चातिदीर्घासु रात्रिषु यथा-सुखं विजह्रुर् इति ॥१९॥ — Then they enjoyed themselves happily for very long nights
19.translation: Not only are they the same senses but also the goddesses, he argues, because they are played with by Krishna. What about the moon? This indicates that the moon was surprised and forgot to go. Then all the previous planets remained in the same place. Then they enjoyed themselves happily for very long nights

20.word_for_word:
किं च, कृत्वेति । — What’s more, it’s done.; अयं भावः--- — This is the sense of; > कात्यायनि महामाये महा-योगिन्य् अधीश्वरि । — > O Katyayani, great illusion, great yogini and master.; >
> नन्द-गोप-सुतं देवि पतिं मे कुरु ते नमः ॥ — >
> O goddess, please make the son of Nanda and Gopa my husband.; [भा।पु। — [Bh.P.; १०.२२.४] — 10.22.4]; इति प्रत्येकं ताभिः प्रार्थनात्, भगवतापि---याताबला व्रजं सिद्धा मयेमा रंस्यथ क्षपाः [भा।पु। — Thus each of them prayed, and the Lord also---Yatabala Vraja perfected, may you enjoy these nights [Bh.p.; १०.२२.२७] इति तथैव प्रतिश्रुतत्वात्, तावन्तम् आत्मानं कृत्वा रेमे इति । — 10.22.27], since it was so promised, that he enjoyed himself so much.; यावतीर् यावत्यः ॥२०॥ — as many as they are.
20.translation:
What’s more, it’s done. This is the sense of > O Katyayani, great illusion, great yogini and master. >
> O goddess, please make the son of Nanda and Gopa my husband. [Bh.P. 10.22.4] Thus each of them prayed, and the Lord also---Yatabala Vraja perfected, may you enjoy these nights [Bh.p. 10.22.27], since it was so promised, that he enjoyed himself so much. as many as they are.

21.word_for_word: कृपातिशयम् आह---तासाम् इति ॥२१॥ — He argues that the excess of compassion is for them.
21.translation: He argues that the excess of compassion is for them.

22.word_for_word: ततोऽतिहृष्टानां गोपीनां चरितम् आह---गोप्य इति । — Then he described the character of the gopīs, who were overjoyed.; स्फुरतां स्वर्ण-कुण्डलानां कुन्तलानां च, त्विषा गण्डेषु या श्रीः, तया सुधितेन अमृतायितेन हास-सहितेन निरीक्षणेन च ऋषभस्य पत्युः कृष्णस्य मानं दधत्यः पूजां कुर्वत्यस् तत्-कर्माणि जगुः । — They honored and worshiped Lord Kṛṣṇa, the husband of the bull, by their sparkling golden earrings and locks, by the beauty that sparkled on their cheeks, and by their observation with a nectar-infused smile.; तस्य कररुहैर् नखैः स्पर्शेन प्रमोदो यासां ताः ॥२२॥ — Those who were delighted by the touch of his palms and nails.
22.translation: Then he described the character of the gopīs, who were overjoyed. They honored and worshiped Lord Kṛṣṇa, the husband of the bull, by their sparkling golden earrings and locks, by the beauty that sparkled on their cheeks, and by their observation with a nectar-infused smile. Those who were delighted by the touch of his palms and nails.

23.word_for_word: अथ जल-केलिम् आह---ताभिर् इति । — Then he said to the water-player, "By them.; तासाम् अङ्ग-सङ्गेन घृष्टा संमर्दिता या स्रक् तस्याः अत एव तासां कुच-कुङ्कुमेन रञ्जितायाः सम्बन्धिभिर् गन्धर्व-पालिभिर् गन्धर्वपा गन्धर्व-पतय इव गायन्तो योऽलयस् तैर् अनुद्रुतोऽनुगतः स कृष्णो वाः उदकम् आविशत् । — The garland, which had been rubbed and crushed by the touch of their limbs, was therefore painted with the saffron of their breasts.; भिन्न-सेतुर् विदारित वप्रः स्वयं चातिक्रान्त-लोक-वेद-मर्यादः ॥२३॥ — The bridge was broken and the bow was torn and he himself had transgressed the boundaries of the Vedas of the world.
23.translation: Then he said to the water-player, "By them. The garland, which had been rubbed and crushed by the touch of their limbs, was therefore painted with the saffron of their breasts. The bridge was broken and the bow was torn and he himself had transgressed the boundaries of the Vedas of the world.

24.word_for_word: स्व-रतिर् आत्मारामोऽपि अत्र गोपी-मण्डलेऽम्भसि वा ॥२४॥ — He is attracted to himself and is self-satisfied here in the circle of gopis or in the water.
24.translation: He is attracted to himself and is self-satisfied here in the circle of gopis or in the water.

25.word_for_word: स्थल-जल-क्रीडे दर्शिते वन-क्रीडां दर्शयति---ततश् चेति । — He shows the forest game shown in the land and water game: and then.; यमुनाया उपवने जल-स्थल-प्रसूनानां गन्धो यस्मिंस् तेनानिलेन जुष्टानि दिशां तटान्य् अन्ता यस्मिन् । — In the garden of the Yamuna, where the fragrance of water, land and flowers is carried, the banks of the Yamuna are blown in all directions.; यद् वा दिशश् च तटं स्थलं च यस्मिन्न् उपवने । — Whatever the direction, the coast, the land in which the garden is located; भृङ्गाणां प्रमदानां च गणैर् आवृतः ॥२५॥ — It was surrounded by flocks of bees and females
25.translation: He shows the forest game shown in the land and water game: and then. In the garden of the Yamuna, where the fragrance of water, land and flowers is carried, the banks of the Yamuna are blown in all directions. Whatever the direction, the coast, the land in which the garden is located It was surrounded by flocks of bees and females

26.word_for_word:
रास-क्रीडां निगमयति---एवम् इति । — He describes the game of Rasa as follows.; स कृष्णः सत्य-सङ्कल्पोऽनुरागि-स्त्री-कदम्ब-स्थ एवं सर्वा निशाः सेवितवान् । — That Kṛṣṇa, true to His resolve, thus spent all nights in the kadamba of a loving woman.; शरत्-काव्य-कथा-रसाश्रयाः शरदि भवाः काव्येषु कथ्यमाना ये रसाः, तेषाम् आश्रय-भूता निशाः । — The nights are the source of the tastes of autumn poetry and stories.; यद् वा, निशा इति द्वितीयाऽत्यन्त-संयोगे। — or, night, in the second extreme conjunction.; शृङ्गार-रसाश्रयाः शरदि प्रसिद्धाः काव्येषु याः कथाः, ताः सिषेवे इति । — The stories in the autumn poems, which are based on aesthetic taste, are said to have been served.; एवम् अप्य् आत्मन्य् एवावरुद्धः सौरतश् चरम-धातुर् न तु स्खलितो यस्येति काम-जयोक्तिः ॥२६-२७॥ — Even thus the ultimate element of Saurata is fixed in the Self but has not slipped away from him, as stated by the conqueror of desire (26-27).; : शरत्-काव्य-कथाः शरदि सर्वदेशकालकविभिर् यावत्यो
वर्णयितुं शक्यन्ते तावतीः कथाः सिषेवे आचचार । — Autumn poetry stories in autumn by poets of all countries and times
There are so many stories that can be described in the service of Sisheva.
26.translation:
He describes the game of Rasa as follows. That Kṛṣṇa, true to His resolve, thus spent all nights in the kadamba of a loving woman. The nights are the source of the tastes of autumn poetry and stories. or, night, in the second extreme conjunction. The stories in the autumn poems, which are based on aesthetic taste, are said to have been served. Even thus the ultimate element of Saurata is fixed in the Self but has not slipped away from him, as stated by the conqueror of desire (26-27). Autumn poetry stories in autumn by poets of all countries and times
There are so many stories that can be described in the service of Sisheva.

28.word_for_word: प्रतीपं प्रतिकूलाधर्मम् इत्य् अर्थः । — This means that the opposite is the opposite religion.; आचरत् कृतवान् । — He conducted and did.; न चेदम् अधर्म-मात्रं कलञ्ज-भक्षणादिवत् किन्तु महा-साहसम् इत्य् आह---पर-दाराभिमर्शनम् इति ॥२८॥ — If this is not merely unrighteousness, as in the case of eating a stigma, but it is a great audacity, he argues, it is to rub another's wife.
28.translation: This means that the opposite is the opposite religion. He conducted and did. If this is not merely unrighteousness, as in the case of eating a stigma, but it is a great audacity, he argues, it is to rub another's wife.

29.word_for_word: आप्त-कामस्य नायम् अधर्म इति चेद् यद्य् एवं कामाभावान् निन्दितं केनाभिप्रायेण कृतवान् इति पृच्छति---आप्त-काम इति ॥ — If one says that one who has fulfilled his desires is not irreligious, then what is the purpose of condemning him for not having lustful desires?; २९ ॥ — 29 ॥
29.translation: If one says that one who has fulfilled his desires is not irreligious, then what is the purpose of condemning him for not having lustful desires? 29 ॥

30.word_for_word: परमेश्वरे कैमुतिक-न्यायेन परिहर्तुं सामान्यतो महतां वृत्तम् आह---धर्म-व्यतिक्रम इति । — To avoid camutic law in God, he argues that the behavior of great men in general is a transgression of religion.; साहसं च दृष्टं प्रजापतीन्द्र-सोम-विश्वामित्रादीनां तच् च तेषां तेजस्विनां दोषाय न भवति ॥३०॥ — The courage of the Prajapatis, Indra, Soma, Vishvamitra and others has been seen and that is not to blame for those brilliant men.
30.translation: To avoid camutic law in God, he argues that the behavior of great men in general is a transgression of religion. The courage of the Prajapatis, Indra, Soma, Vishvamitra and others has been seen and that is not to blame for those brilliant men.

31.word_for_word: तर्हि यद् यद् आचरति श्रेष्ठः [गीता ३.२१] इति न्यायेन अन्योऽपि कुर्याद् इत्य् आशङ्क्याह---नैतद् इति । — Then, doubting that whatever the best does [Gita 3.21] should be done by another, he says, “This is not so.”; अनीश्वरो देहादि-परतन्त्रः यथा रुद्र-व्यतिरिक्तो विषम् आचरन् भक्षयन् ॥३१॥ — He is without god and is independent of the body and other things, just as a person other than Rudra is acting and eating poison.
31.translation: Then, doubting that whatever the best does [Gita 3.21] should be done by another, he says, “This is not so.” He is without god and is independent of the body and other things, just as a person other than Rudra is acting and eating poison.

32.word_for_word: कथं तर्हि सद्-आचारस्य प्रामाण्यम् अत आह---ईश्वराणाम् इति । — How, then, is the authenticity of good conduct?; तेषां वचः सत्यम्, अतस् तद् उक्तम् आचरेद् एव । — Their words are true, so one should do what they say.; आचरितं तु क्वचित् सत्यम् । — The practice, however, is sometimes true.; अतः स्व-वचो-युक्तं तेषां वचसा यद् यद् युक्तम् अविरुद्धं तत् तद् एवाचरेत् ॥३२॥ — Therefore whatever is in accordance with his own words and not contrary to their words should be done.
32.translation: How, then, is the authenticity of good conduct? Their words are true, so one should do what they say. The practice, however, is sometimes true. Therefore whatever is in accordance with his own words and not contrary to their words should be done.

33.word_for_word: ननु तर्हि तेऽपि किम् एवं साहसम् आचरन्ति तत्राह---कुशलेति । — If so, why do they also dare to do so?; प्रारब्ध-कर्म-क्षपण-मात्रम् एव तेषां कृत्यं नान्यद् इत्य् अर्थः ॥३३॥ — This means that their duty is only to destroy the actions they have started and nothing else.
33.translation: If so, why do they also dare to do so? This means that their duty is only to destroy the actions they have started and nothing else.

34.word_for_word: प्रस्तुतम् आह---किम् उतेति । — The presenter said, "What is Ute?"; कुशलाकुशलान्वयो न विद्यत इति किं पुनर् वक्तव्यम् इत्य् अर्थः ॥३४॥ — What more can be said about the fact that there is no consequence between the good and the bad, this means.
34.translation: The presenter said, "What is Ute?" What more can be said about the fact that there is no consequence between the good and the bad, this means.

35.word_for_word: एतद् एव स्फुटीकरोति---यस्य पाद-पङ्कज-परागस्य निषेवणेन तृप्ताः । — This is what it crystallizes: they are satisfied with serving the pollen of His lotus feet.; यद् वा, यस्य पाद-पङ्कज-परागे निषेवा येषां, ते च ते तृप्ताश् चेति भक्ता इत्य् अर्थः । — That is, they are devotees who are satisfied with the pollen of His lotus feet.; तथा ज्ञानिनश् च न नह्यमाना बन्धनम् अप्राप्तवन्तः ॥ — Similarly, the wise, who were not carried away, did not attain bondage.; ३५ — 35
35.translation: This is what it crystallizes: they are satisfied with serving the pollen of His lotus feet. That is, they are devotees who are satisfied with the pollen of His lotus feet. Similarly, the wise, who were not carried away, did not attain bondage. 35

36.word_for_word: पर-दारत्वं गोपीनाम् अङ्गीकृत्य परिहृतम् । — The gopīs accepted that they were the wives of others and avoided them.; इदानीं भगवतः सर्वान्तर्यामिणः पर-दार-सेवा नाम न काचिद् इत्य् आह---गोपीनाम् इति । — Now he argues that there is no such thing as service to the wives of others, the omniscient Lord, and that it is the service of the gopis.; योऽन्तश् चरत्य् अध्यक्षो बुद्ध्य्-आदि-साक्षी, स एव क्रीडनेन देह-भाक्, न त्व् अस्मद्-आदि-तुल्यो येन दोषः स्याद् इति ॥३६॥ — He who moves within, the presiding being, the witness of intelligence and other things, is the one who enjoys the body by play, but he is not equal to us and other things, so that there is no fault.
36.translation: The gopīs accepted that they were the wives of others and avoided them. Now he argues that there is no such thing as service to the wives of others, the omniscient Lord, and that it is the service of the gopis. He who moves within, the presiding being, the witness of intelligence and other things, is the one who enjoys the body by play, but he is not equal to us and other things, so that there is no fault.

37.word_for_word: नन्व् एवं चेद् आप्त-कामस्य निन्दिते कुतः प्रवृत्तिः ? — If so, where is the instinct in condemning the attained desire?; इत्य् अत आह---अनुग्रहायेति । — It is therefore argued that it is for the sake of grace.; शृङ्गार-रसाकृष्ट-चेतसोऽतिबहिर्मुखान् अपि स्व-परान् कर्तुम् इति भावः ॥३७॥ — This means that even those whose minds are attracted to the taste of aesthetics are very outwardly oriented towards their own and others.
37.translation: If so, where is the instinct in condemning the attained desire? It is therefore argued that it is for the sake of grace. This means that even those whose minds are attracted to the taste of aesthetics are very outwardly oriented towards their own and others.

38.word_for_word: नन्व् अन्येऽपि भिन्नाचाराः स्व-चेष्टितम् एवम् एवेति वदन्ति ? — Do other different customs say that their behavior is the same?; तत्राह---नासूयन्न् इति । — There he says, "They did not envy.; एवं-भूतैश्वर्याभावे तथा कुर्वन्तः पापा ज्ञेया इति भावः ॥३७॥ — Thus, in the absence of the power of beings, those who do so are to be understood as sinners.
38.translation: Do other different customs say that their behavior is the same? There he says, "They did not envy. Thus, in the absence of the power of beings, those who do so are to be understood as sinners.

39.word_for_word: ब्रह्म-रात्रे ब्राह्मे मुहूर्ते उपावृत्ते प्राप्ते ॥३८॥ — When the Brahma-night and the Brahma-muhurta have arrived.
39.translation: When the Brahma-night and the Brahma-muhurta have arrived.

40.word_for_word:
भगवतः काम-विजय-रूप-रास-क्रीडा-श्रवणादेः काम-विजयम् एव फलम् आह---विक्रीडितम् इति । — He argues that the fruit of the Lord’s conquest of desire, form, passion, play, hearing, etc., is the conquest of desire, and that it is played.; अचिरेण धीरः सन् हृद्-रोगं कामम् आशु अपहिनोति परित्यजतीति ॥४०॥ — Soon, being steadfast, he quickly gets rid of the disease of the heart and gives up desire.; : यद् वा कामं यथेष्टं आशु भक्तिं लब्ध्वा कामादि-सर्व-हृद्रोगम्
अचिरेण हिनोतीत्य् अर्थः । — Or whatever desire, having attained devotion as quickly as desired, all diseases of the heart, such as desire
It means that he will soon destroy.
40.translation:
He argues that the fruit of the Lord’s conquest of desire, form, passion, play, hearing, etc., is the conquest of desire, and that it is played. Soon, being steadfast, he quickly gets rid of the disease of the heart and gives up desire. Or whatever desire, having attained devotion as quickly as desired, all diseases of the heart, such as desire
It means that he will soon destroy.
